new.s: Which language did the Yadavas of Devagiri use as the language of scholarship?
new.x: The Yadavas spoke Marathi, but Sanskrit was their language of scholarship.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Yadavas of Devagiri:
1. Their mother tongue was Marathi.
2. They made Telugu their court language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Yadavas' mother tongue was Marathi and they encouraged it; Telugu was not their court language.

new.s: In which battle did the Pandyas defeat Ganapatideva in 1263?
new.x: In 1263 the Pandyas defeated Ganapatideva at Muttukur (Muthukuru).

new.s: Which part of the Kakatiya kingdom fell to the Pandyas after the battle of Muttukur (1263)?
new.x: After the Pandyas beat Ganapatideva at Muttukur in 1263, Nellore passed to them.

new.s: Who among the following were the first overlords of the Kakatiyas?
new.x: The Kakatiyas first served the Rashtrakutas and later the Kalyani Chalukyas.

new.s: Under which dynasty did the Kakatiyas serve as feudatories after the Rashtrakuta phase?
new.x: After the Rashtrakutas, the Kakatiyas served the Kalyani Chalukyas as Mahamandaleswaras.

new.s: Which Kakatiya ruler united the Telugu-speaking lands into one 'Telugudesam'?
new.x: Ganapatideva, the greatest Kakatiya, ruled 63 years and united Telugudesam.
new.angle: U0093 PYQ ye66d2a2a9dc unifier of Andhradesa

new.s: After which dynasty were the Kakatiyas the second to unify all the Telugu-speaking regions?
new.x: The Kakatiyas were the second dynasty after the Satavahanas to unify all Telugu-speaking regions.
new.angle: U0093 PYQ ye66d2a2a9dc unification of Andhradesa

new.s: Ulugh Khan, who took Prataparudra captive in 1323, later became which Sultan?
new.x: Ulugh Khan (Juna Khan), the captor of Prataparudra, later ruled as Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
new.angle: U0094 #8 / PYQ y8420a397ecd captor of Prataparudra

new.s: Under which Sultan did Ulugh Khan lead the final siege of Warangal in 1323?
new.x: The 1323 conquest of Warangal was led by Ulugh Khan for his father, Sultan Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq.

new.s: Agastya, a court poet of Prataparudra II, is identified with which author?
new.x: Historians identify Vidyanatha, author of Prataparudra Yashobhushanam, with Agastya.

new.s: Which poetess, the author of Madhura Vijayam, was a disciple of Agastya?
new.x: Gangadevi, who wrote Madhura Vijayam, was a disciple of Agastya.

new.s: Which samaya of the Kakatiya period was a guild of agricultural farmers?
new.x: Chitrameli was the samaya (shreni) of agricultural farmers, not of merchants.

new.s: Who were the members of the Chitrameli in the Kakatiya period?
new.x: The Chitrameli was a farmers' samaya; Nanadesis were foreign merchants and Nakaram domestic merchants.

new.s: In Kakatiya trade, who were the 'Ubhaya Nanadesi' merchants?
o: Merchants of both the Desis, Paradesis and Nanadesis
new.x: Ubhaya Nanadesi means 'both': it took in merchants of the Desis, Paradesis and Nanadesis.

new.s: Desiyakonda Pattanam was another name of which Kakatiya port?
new.x: Motupalli, the chief Kakatiya port, was also called Desiyakonda (Deseeyakkonda) Pattanam.
new.angle: U0095 #17 / PYQ y0ddee7b7ae9 Motupalli other name

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Kakatiya ports:
1. Motupalli was also called Desiyakonda Pattanam.
2. Hamsaladeevi lay on the Nellore coast.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Motupalli was Desiyakonda Pattanam; Hamsaladeevi was in the Krishna delta, while Krishnapatnam was on the Nellore coast.
new.angle: U0095 #2 / PYQ y5cddb6b388e Motupalli other name

new.s: According to Sakala Neeti Sammatamu, who were the Ashtadasa Tirthas of the Kakatiya state?
o: The eighteen occupational groups inside the Warangal fort
The eighteen sacred tanks of the kingdom
The eighteen spies of the king
The eighteen high officers (ministers) of state
new.x: The Ashtadasa Tirthas were the 18 high officers or ministers of the state.

new.s: How many tirthas (high officers of state) were there under the Kakatiyas according to Sakala Neeti Sammatamu?
new.x: Sakala Neeti Sammatamu names 18 tirthas (Ashtadasa Tirthas); 12 were Ayagars, 72 Niyogas and 77 Nayankaras.

new.s: Who among the following was one of the Siddhatraya among the Aradhya acharyas?
new.x: The Siddhatraya were Revana, Marula and Ekorama; Manchana, Sripati and Mallikarjuna belong to another triad.

new.s: Into how many triads were the twelve Aradhya acharyas grouped?
new.x: The 12 Aradhya acharyas were grouped in four triads, such as the Siddhatraya and the Panditatraya.

new.s: From which Shaiva sect did the Kapalikas emerge as an offshoot?
new.x: The Kapalikas, skull-bowl ascetics, grew out of the Pasupata sect.

new.s: Which of the following was a Kalamukha (Shaiva) centre in the Kakatiya period?
new.x: Alampur was a Kalamukha/Shaiva centre; Kolanupaka, Bodhan and Patancheru were Jain centres.
